sections.heading: Who should buy and who should skip
paragraphs: Buy a wings-focused air fryer if you cook wings weekly and care about crisp skin without a deep fryer — especially if you want Hi-Fry / MaxCrisp heat or a bigger basket for game day.
Skip oversized dual-zone or oven combos if you only make a small batch once a month and counter space is tight.
bullets: Weeknight 1–2 lb batches → 5–6.5 qt basket fryers
Family 2–3 lb batches → 8 qt Hi-Fry / MaxCrisp models
Party / two flavors → DualZone or large dual-basket units

sections.heading: What matters for air fryer chicken wings
paragraphs: Wings need dry heat and room for air to move. Overcrowding softens skin; underpowered baskets take longer and cook unevenly.
Look for high max temps, crisp-boost presets, and a basket you will actually wash after sticky sauces.
bullets: Leave space between pieces — cook in batches if needed
Pat wings dry and toss lightly before cooking
Sauce after crisping for the best texture

faqs.question: What size air fryer is best for chicken wings?
faqs.answer: A 5–6.5 qt basket handles about 1.5–2 lb for weeknights. Choose 8 qt or DualZone / dual-basket models for family or party batches so wings are not stacked.

faqs.question: How do I get crispy air fryer chicken wings?
faqs.answer: Pat wings dry, avoid overcrowding, cook hot enough for your model, and sauce after the skin crisps. Shake or flip halfway for even browning.

faqs.question: Is DualZone better for wings?
faqs.answer: DualZone or dual-basket units help when you want two flavors, staggered timing, or larger total capacity. A strong single basket is simpler if you only cook one batch at a time.

faqs.question: Do I need a special wings preset?
faqs.answer: Presets are convenient, but temperature and time control matter more. High-heat or Hi-Fry / MaxCrisp modes help when you want extra crunch.
